Subject: MSA redlines + on-prem addendum request (Novamed)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal reviewed the MSA and the order form and have a handful of redlines specifically tied to the proposed on-prem deployment we plan for our clinical analytics environment. High-level asks: 

- Clarify license scope for on-prem: do we get production-use rights for the deployed model artifacts or limited runtime tokens only?
- Operator access / witness requirement: we need an evidence/witnessing mechanism for snapshots and a defined audit window for Novamed auditors.
- Escrow-like assurance: we prefer either a sealed snapshot deposit or a quarterly signed attestation plus validated snapshot retention for 12 months.
- Data handling: confirmation on backups, retention, and whether Redwood will have any remote access to live patient data in the on-prem environment.

I've attached Novamed_MSA_Redlines_20260803.pdf with inline comments. Can you route to legal and ops and let us know what options Redwood is willing to accept? We need a redline response by COB Friday to stay on our vendor selection timeline.

Appreciate your help — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Team — forwarding Novamed's redlines for the on-prem order. Running list of constraints from them and my initial thoughts inline: 

- License scope: customer wants production-use rights for the deployed artifacts. Our typical stance is runtime-only for hosted; for on-prem we can offer a restricted binary distribution license limited to the agreed deployment image and instance count + audit logs.
- Operator access / witness: they want a witnessing mechanism. Proposed alternatives:
  1) Sealed snapshot deposit to an escrow agent (customer-preferred)
  2) Quarterly witnessed snapshot + signed attestation by Redwood ops (lower lift)
  3) Time-bound remote console for a monitored audit window (very controlled, ephemeral)
- Escrow-like assurance: if escrow is non-starter legally, propose Option 2 + cryptographic hash of snapshots uploaded to a mutually controlled S3 bucket (read-only for Novamed).
- Data handling: must confirm no persistent remote access to live patient data; remote access only for emergency hotline with pre-authorized runbooks and logged sessions.

Action items: Laura/David, can you review the attached and suggest redline language for (a) addendum defining "Licensed Runtime Image", (b) operator access / witness options and witness wording, (c) indemnity/forensics carveouts. Also please flag commercial implications if we accept sealed snapshot escrow.

I've attached an initial draft (privdeploy_addendum_draft_v1.docx) with placeholders for the options above. Novamed expects response by COB Fri (2026-08-06).

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA redlines + on-prem addendum request (Novamed)

Karthik / team — reviewed Novamed's redlines and drafted a focused set of redline options. Key legal positions: 

1) License scope: we can offer a "Licensed Runtime Image" grant limited to the specific SHA-tagged image(s) delivered under the order form, for use on Novamed-managed infrastructure, subject to the maximum instances and territory on the order form. We should avoid granting a broad perpetual copy-right style license.

2) Operator access & witnessing: accept "Option 2" as primary: quarterly witnessed snapshot + signed attestation. Language: "Provider will generate a read-only, cryptographically-hashed snapshot of the deployed runtime and associated configuration, witnessed by Provider's authorized representative in the presence of Customer's designated witness or via a mutually agreed third-party auditor. Provider will retain copies for 12 months and provide hash receipts to Customer."

3) Escrow / sealed deposit: avoid direct escrow of binaries into a third-party vault (risk & cost). If customer insists, mark-up: escrow only as a last-resort contingent on shared acceptance testing and a technical understanding statement; require fees and limited release triggers.

4) Remote access and data handling: accept "no persistent remote access"; allow emergency remote access for incident response with pre-authorized runbook and two-person approval (customer security lead + Redwood ops) and explicit logging. Add requirement for redaction of PHI in any debug artifacts before sharing.

5) Forensics and indemnity: we can accept narrow forensic access carveouts for investigating security incidents; carve out for customer-mandated forensics must require substantiation and an NDA Addendum.

I've prepared MSA_addendum_redline_20260805.docx with tracked changes and two language options for each of the above points (preferred and fallback). David — please add ops feasibility notes for the witnessed snapshot process and any runbook templates we should attach. Marissa — please draft a short commercial note on potential pricing uplift for on-prem licensing + escrow services.

We'll aim to combine into a single redline response to Novamed by EOD Fri.

Laura Bennett

Subject: Proposed redline approach & next steps — Novamed on‑prem addendum

Emma / Tom — thanks for the patience. Quick summary of what we can offer and next steps. See attached redline (MSA_addendum_redline_20260805.docx) for tracked language. Highlights: 

- License: we will grant a Limited Licensed Runtime Image (SHA-tagged) for production use on Novamed-managed infra. This is not a general-purpose perpetual copy license — limited instance counts and territory remain in the order form.
- Witnessing / escrow: we propose a two-track compromise: 
  • Primary: Quarterly witnessed snapshot with cryptographic hash receipts retained by Redwood for 12 months; Customer may provide a witness or we can use an agreed third-party auditor.
  • Fallback: If Novamed requires escrow deposit into a third-party vault, we need a separate Escrow Exhibit, fees, and clear release triggers — we can provide language but prefer the quarterly witness approach operationally.
- Remote access: no persistent remote access to live systems without explicit approval. Emergency access allowed via pre-authorized runbook, two approvals, session recording, and PHI redaction.

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached redline and indicate whether the quarterly witnessed snapshot + hash receipts meet your risk requirements.
2) If you are open to the witness option, we'll schedule a technical sync next week to walk the runbook and define the witness process (30–45 min).
3) If Novamed insists on escrow, we'll circulate an Escrow Exhibit and commercial fee schedule.
